scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: A single IT Department workstation, it_lab3 (192.168.1.x),
"is totally isolated" -- the user says it can't reach anything at all, not even its
own gateway, and suspects the machine lost its network or its switch port died.
Please find and confirm the fault on it_lab3 and tell us what to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: Every layer of the diagnostic sweep was run against it_lab3 and the surrounding fabric and came back clean. At Layer 2, l2_snapshot confirmed all 30 devices have intact, UP interfaces with no duplicate MACs and no missing links — including it_lab3's eth0. At Layer 3, it_lab3 holds the correct address (192.168.1.5/24) with a valid default route to 192.168.1.1, and live pings proved it reaches its gateway with 0% loss (3/3 packets), cross-subnet hosts (office_pc at 192.168.3.2, 0% loss), and internet-side hosts (128.168.0.2, 0% loss). Reciprocal probes from it_lab1 to it_lab3 also succeed. The fabric-wide helpers found no ACL drop rules, no tc shaping, no resource pressure, and no flap or stress processes on any device. The carrier_changes counter on it_lab3's eth0 reads 2, which is the startup-only baseline in Kathara (one down/up transition at container initialisation) and is accompanied by no flap script, no "Network is down" log entries, and no suspicious DHCP/link history. The OSPF daemon is inactive on all three routers, but this is consistent with the statically-routed topology — FRR zebra is running and inter-subnet forwarding works end-to-end. In short, no fault is active or traceable on it_lab3: the workstation has full IP connectivity at this moment, and there is no evidence of a mechanism that could have produced transient isolation. The helpdesk ticket claim is unconfirmed; no corrective action is warranted.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 holds the correct IP (192.168.1.5/24) and successfully pings its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss (3/3), confirming baseline health.
